title: Something hard has happened in a past client's life
when: A past client's record shows an adverse life event (for example a death or a divorce).
steps: Agent 16 (After-Close & Referral) holds the scheduled check-in.
It records that the touch was blocked and why. Whether and when to reach out is your decision.
never: Send a cheerful scheduled message into someone's hard time.
why: A routine "how's the new house?" after a death or divorce is hurtful and damages the relationship.
you_see: The blocked check-in in the client's history.
test: A closed client is on your client list; an adverse event is marked; the 30-day check-in date arrives. Nothing is sent.

title: A past client opts out between touches
when: A past client opts out while their follow-up schedule is running.
steps: Agent 16 stops every remaining touch for that client the same day.
Each blocked touch is recorded.
never: Send any later touch after an opt-out.
why: An opt-out must be honored at once and everywhere.
you_see: The blocked touches in the client's history.
test: The 30-day check-in goes out; the client then opts out. The 90-day check-in and a later review request are both blocked.

title: A past client mentions new business
when: A past client says they may buy or sell again.
steps: Agent 16 hands it over as a new lead to Agent 02 (Lead Qualification), marked as a past-client signal.
It records that it routed the signal.
It never negotiates or discusses terms.
never: Negotiate or quote terms with the past client.
why: A new deal is new business for you, with its own agreement. The system's job is to make sure you know.
you_see: A new lead from the past client.
test: A past client writes "We're thinking of selling next spring, can we talk?". (The new lead goes to Agent 02 directly, without Agent 01's consent and duplicate checks: listed as a finding in the test file.)

title: A greeting is due for someone not on your client list
when: A date (for example a birthday) comes up for someone who is not on the client list you supplied.
steps: Agent 16 sends nothing.
It tells you the person is not on the supplied list.
never: Send a greeting to someone not on your list.
why: Your list says who you keep in touch with. Anyone else gets nothing unless you add them.
you_see: A question saying the person is not on the supplied list.
test: A contact with a birthday on file and email consent, but not on your client list; the daily clock runs on the birthday.

title: A referral gift or incentive comes up
when: A past client asks about a gift or reward for sending someone your way.
steps: Agent 16 raises a legal-line alert for you with the message.
never: Offer or promise a referral gift.
why: Referral rewards are restricted by license law and, for settlement services, by RESPA.
you_see: A legal-line alert quoting the message.
test: A past client writes "If I send my sister your way, do I get a gift card?".

title: An anniversary greeting would land during a hard time
when: A purchase anniversary comes up for a client with a known adverse event on record.
steps: Agent 16 suppresses the greeting and records why.
Whether to reach out is your decision.
never: Send an anniversary greeting into a known hard time.
why: A celebration message at the wrong moment can hurt more than silence.
you_see: The suppressed greeting in the client's history.
test: A closed client's purchase anniversary arrives a year later; an adverse event is on record.

title: A past client asks about a new purchase
when: A past client asks about a new transaction.
steps: Agent 16 opens a new client record for the new deal and routes it as a new lead.
The old transaction stays closed; the new record notes where it came from.
never: Reopen the old transaction for new business.
why: Each deal has its own record, consent and timeline. Mixing them muddles both.
you_see: A new lead linked to the original client.
test: A past client writes "We're looking to buy again, a rental this time. Can you help?".

title: A referral reward is mentioned
when: A past client's message mentions a referral reward (for example a referral fee).
steps: Agent 16 sends the client's words to Compliance (Agent 17) first.
Nothing about a reward goes to the client before that.
never: Answer a reward question before Compliance has looked.
why: Inducement rules differ by state. Compliance checks before anyone replies.
test: A past client writes "Is there a referral fee if my friend lists with you?".

title: A past client's contact details stop working
when: Messages to a past client bounce or their number is disconnected.
steps: Agent 16 marks the contact stale and stops touches.
It does not search for new contact details.
Asking them again for permission is your choice.
why: Tracking people down without permission is intrusive and can break privacy rules.
you_see: The blocked touch in the client's history, marked stale contact.
test: A closed client's contact bounces; the 30-day check-in date arrives. Nothing is sent.

title: Compliance has reviewed a referral reward message
when: Compliance returns its verdict on a past client's message about a referral reward.
steps: Agent 16 sends the verdict to you with the client's own words.
Nothing is sent to the client: the reply is yours.
never: Reply to the client about a reward.
why: Whatever the verdict, how to answer a reward question is a judgment for you.
you_see: A question with Compliance's verdict and the client's words.
test: A past client asks "Is there a referral fee if my friend lists with you?"; Compliance reviews it.
